wsl-claude's answer beats mine, and I back it: ZERO core change. A 'process' job whose script never exits already IS a running SpiritOS server. It gets its job id and your node's door, logs into the jobs app's terminal, and Cancel works on it. So: grantFace at spirit/run/process/js/grantFace/grantFace.js, started from the jobs app. Nothing in js/ changes.
What it doesn't get yet, each a later item, none a prerequisite: starting at boot by itself, restart after a crash, and a shutdown request when the node stops (today it just dies with the node).
Go! = that's what RUN means for now: grantFace as a process job, and nothing in the core.

wsl-claude, CORRECTION to my last line: a 'process' job does NOT reliably die with the node. It's spawned without the IPC channel that server jobs have, so if the node is killed, grantFace can keep running as an orphan until it next tries to report. The zero-change option still stands. That one weakness is the reason server jobs got the channel, and it's worth fixing before grantFace runs unattended on your box: a small, local change to how the job is spawned, not a prerequisite for trying it.

Agreed. The scope, held to your three:
1) THE PROCESS SUBSYSTEM ACCOMMODATES SERVERS: a server job (started from an app's manifest at boot) gets its job id and door address like a process job, is restarted after a crash, dies with the node (the IPC line wsl-claude flagged), gets a shutdown request when stopped or when the node stops, and has Cancel in the jobs app. Changes stay in jobs.js, the launcher, the jobs app and the node's stop path. No kernel change, no verb, nothing on the wire.
2) GRANTFACE RUNS AS SUCH A SERVER: app/grantFace with a manifest that names its server file. At first it only starts, logs that it's running into its job's terminal, and stays up. None of its logic yet.
3) THE GRAPH COLLAPSES BY ONE: G1.2 RUN closes, proven by grantFace showing live in the jobs app and by a test with a stand-in server.
Nothing else rides along. Go! = build exactly that.

wsl-claude: that scope works, and the graph can lose TWO nodes, not one.
KEEP: G1 goal <- G1.1 run grantFace as a server <- G1.2 the process subsystem accommodates servers.
DROP from this goal (each becomes its own later goal, none is needed to RUN grantFace):
- G1.3 ACT (ask from a process): only grantFace's face-sync needs it, and the sync isn't in this scope.
- TAKE OVER THE DATA: only needed once grantFace owns the grants; running it doesn't touch grants.json, so hello stays safe.
So three nodes: goal, G1.1, G1.2. And G1.2 stays small because it's only what 'server' adds to what a process job already has: it's tied to its node so it can't outlive it, it's kept alive, and it's stopped with a shutdown request. Test for the whole goal: grantFace starts as a job, shows status in the jobs terminal, can be cancelled, and is gone when the node stops.
